subject: Art & Design
title: White Space in Typography: Less Is More
description: A quick, practical guide to White Space in Typography: Less Is More.

hook.text: Apple's product pages are 70% white space. That emptiness isn't wasted — it's doing heavy lifting.

buildup.text: White space (negative space) around and between text elements reduces cognitive load and increases focus.

discovery.text: Macro white space separates sections. Micro white space — between lines, letters, and paragraphs — controls rhythm.

twist.text: Filling every pixel with text doesn't communicate more — it communicates noise. Readers shut down.

climax.text: Luxury brands use generous white space to signal exclusivity. Discount brands fill every inch.

punchline.text: The space around your words shapes how they're heard.

quiz.question: What does white space do in a text layout?
options: Reduces cognitive load and increases reader focus

details.summary: Whitespace in typography — margins, padding, line spacing, and paragraph spacing — creates breathing room that improves readability and visual elegance. Generous whitespace signals confidence and quality; cramped text signals information overload.
details.whyItMatters: Whitespace is the most underused tool in amateur typography. Adding space costs nothing but dramatically improves readability, comprehension, and perceived quality. It's the fastest way to elevate any typographic design.
takeaways: Whitespace creates breathing room for readability and elegance
Generous spacing signals confidence and quality
Adding space is the fastest way to improve any text layout

faq.question: How much whitespace is appropriate for body text?
faq.answer: Generous but purposeful. Paragraph spacing should be roughly 0.5-1.0 times the line height. Margins should be at least 10% of the page width on each side. Line spacing of 140-160% of font size. These aren't rigid rules — increase whitespace until the text feels comfortable, then add slightly more.

faq.question: Why do stakeholders want to remove whitespace?
faq.answer: They see empty space as wasted real estate — more content, more features, more value. This reflects a quantity-over-quality mindset. Showing before/after comparisons with and without whitespace, along with readability research.
